analysis.investment_thesis: Aegis Vopak owns genuinely scarce infrastructure (LPG/chemical terminals) with strong JV parentage, but ROCE of 7.01% and ROE of 8.73% fail every basic quality test Munger demands. At 109x earnings and 55x EV/EBITDA for a capital-intensive tollbooth earning sub-cost-of-capital returns, the price is divorced from the economics.
key_strengths: Scarce port-terminal infrastructure with regulatory barriers and 48% operating margins
Strong parentage via Aegis Logistics + Royal Vopak JV brings operating know-how
OCF turned solidly positive (INR 478 Cr in 2025) with FCF of INR 350 Cr post-IPO
key_risks: ROCE 7.01% sits below cost of capital — value-destroying at current invested-capital base
Valuation absurd: 109x P/E, 55x EV/EBITDA for a slow-compounding infra asset
Finance cost INR 193 Cr exceeds net profit INR 127 Cr — leverage masks weak unit economics
red_flags: Only 2 years of meaningful operating history; 3Y finance-cost CAGR of 478%
Cumulative investing outflow ~INR 3,100 Cr over 4 years vs modest PAT — extreme capital intensity
Equity ballooned from 997 to 4,742 Cr in 2025 (IPO dilution) yet ROE still single digit
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Inverting first: what kills this investment? Paying 55x EBITDA for an asset earning 7% on capital guarantees a poor outcome unless returns structurally double or the market keeps paying a fantasy multiple. Both are hopes, not theses. Munger's rule — a great business at fair price — is violated twice: returns aren't great (ROCE 7%, ROE 8.7%, both below a risk-free G-Sec equivalent benchmark), and price isn't fair. The 99% gross margin is a red herring typical of asset-leasing models; real economics sit in depreciation + interest, which consume the bulk of EBITDA (EBITDA 584 Cr vs PAT 127 Cr).

This is not a bad business — Indian terminal infrastructure is genuinely moated and Royal Vopak brings world-class discipline. Post-IPO deleveraging plus capacity ramp could push ROCE toward low-teens over 3-5 years. But at INR 22,244 Cr market cap on INR 127 Cr profit, the market is already pricing that optimistic scenario and more. I'd want ROCE sustained above 15%, FCF normalized, and the multiple cut in half before this is interesting. Into the too-hard/too-expensive pile; revisit after the next capex cycle completes.
